title: Cremini, Marsala and Thyme Pan Gravy
description: Finely chopped creminis simmer with thyme and dry Marsala before being blended into a rich mushroom gravy.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain meat-and-bone broth without a vegetable seasoning blend.

steps.title: Caramelize the shallot
steps.text: Soften {shallot} in {oil} in the HexClad over medium-low for 12–16 minutes. Stir often, using splashes of {broth} to keep the shallot moist until soft and deep gold.

steps.title: Simmer the mushrooms
steps.text: Move the skillet off the burner to add {marsala}, then add {mushrooms}, {thyme} and the remaining {broth}. Return to medium-low heat, cover and simmer 6–8 minutes until the mushrooms are very tender.

steps.title: Puree the gravy base
steps.text: Remove the thyme. Blend the hot mixture in a deep heatproof jug until smooth and strain it back into the skillet.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with cream cheese
steps.text: Off heat, whisk {cheese} with a spoonful of warm gravy, then blend it back into the pan. Divide the gravy between the plates or ladle it over mashed potatoes.

notes: Make ahead: Blend the mushroom base up to a day ahead and refrigerate. Keep finished gravy chilled for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the base for up to 2 months and add cream cheese after reheating for a smooth finish. Fridge reheat: Warm in the HexClad over medium-low, stirring with a splash of water or broth if needed. Bring the whole sauce briefly to a rolling boil, then serve. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Whisk smooth and follow the fridge reheating directions. Option A includes Marsala. For a gentler, alcohol-free Option B, replace it with additional plain broth. For dairy-free gravy omit the cream cheese and rely on the mushroom puree and slurry.
